cards.text: Jesus is still teaching His disciples (Luke 6:20), and He's just told them, 'Do not judge, and you will not be judged.' (Luke 6:37) Now He tells them a parable, and it opens with a question: 'Can a blind man lead a blind man?' Friend, I can't find my rolling pin with the lights ON, so who's following ME in the dark?

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, what happens when a blind man leads a blind man?

answers.text: They both fall into a pit
They both wait by the road

cards.text: Next, Jesus talks about a disciple and his teacher. Picture the new baker on day one, flour on his eyebrows, watching the head baker's every move.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says a disciple is above his teacher.
Jesus says everyone who is fully ___ will be like his ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks why you'd look at the speck in your brother's eye. A SPECK, friend? I've had bigger crumbs fall out of this mustache.

cards.question: While you look at the speck in your brother's eye, what does Jesus say you fail to notice in your own eye?

cards.text: Then Jesus pictures someone saying, 'Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,' with that beam still in his own. That's me telling you there's a little dust on your apron while I'm standing here COVERED head to toe in flour.

cards.question: What does Jesus call someone who offers to take out his brother's speck but can't see the beam in his own eye?
True or false: Jesus says to take the beam out of your own eye first, and then you'll see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.

cards.text: Now Jesus switches pictures, from eyes to trees. Friend, the closest I've ever come to a tree is a wooden spoon.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says a bad tree can still bear good fruit.
Jesus says each tree is known by its own ___.

cards.text: Jesus says figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles. You don't fill a tray with chocolate chip dough and open the oven to find sugar cookies.

cards.question: Then Jesus moves from trees to people. Where does the good man bring good things out of?

answers.text: The good treasure of his heart
The good work of his hands
The good store in his house

cards.text: And the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. Then Jesus connects what's in the heart to what comes out when we talk.

cards.question: Jesus says out of the overflow of the heart the ___ speaks.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks one more question, and friend, this one goes straight to the heart. I felt it all the way down in my handle.

cards.question: Jesus asks why people call Him 'Lord, Lord,' but then what?

cards.text: Jesus has one more picture for His sermon. He's going to show what someone is like who comes to Him, hears His words and acts on them.

cards.question: Who does Jesus say the person who hears His words and acts on them is like?

cards.text: This builder doesn't cut corners. He digs down deep, and I mean DEEP, like me digging for the last chocolate chip at the bottom of the bag.

cards.question: The builder who dug down deep laid his foundation on the ___.

cards.text: Then the flood comes, and the torrent crashes right against that house. Friend, I'd be hiding behind the biggest oven I own.

cards.question: True or false: the torrent shakes the house built on the rock.
Why can't the torrent shake the house on the rock?

cards.text: Now the other builder. He hears Jesus' words too, but he doesn't act on them.

cards.question: Jesus says the one who hears and doesn't act is like a man who built his house on ground without a ___.

cards.text: Then the torrent crashes against his house too. Friend, I can't even look.

cards.question: What happens when the torrent crashes against the house without a foundation?

cards.text: Both houses got hit by a torrent, but only one fell, and great was its destruction. The difference is whether the builder acted on Jesus' words, like the gap between reading a recipe and actually turning on the oven.

findings.problem: The second blank's answer, 'teacher', is already given away by card 3 ('Next, Jesus talks about a disciple and his teacher'). The baker doesn't have to reason it out, so it doesn't test anything.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The choice card tells a new turn in the passage itself ('Then Jesus moves from trees to people'). The card before it (card 14) is about figs and grapes and never sets up the move to people. That setup belongs on a story card.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Then Jesus connects what's in the heart to what comes out when we talk' points straight to 'mouth' and rules out 'mind' and 'spirit' for card 17.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card drops the 'like' from the comparison and has the builder himself hearing Jesus' words ('Now the other builder. He hears Jesus' words too'). In Luke 6:49 it's the one who hears and doesn't act who 'is like a man who built his house.' The builder never hears anything.

'The difference is whether the builder acted on Jesus' words' drops the 'like' from Luke 6:47-49. In the text, the one who hears and acts is like the builder. The builders themselves don't act on Jesus' words.
Most of this card repeats what earlier cards already told: both houses were hit by the torrent, and only one fell. The only new detail is 'great was its destruction.'
The card cites Luke 6:49 but also uses Luke 6:47 (acting on Jesus' words) and Luke 6:48 (the first house standing against the torrent). The citation should be Luke 6:47-49.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
